docs.text: MAR-40 Data Sources and Cohort Registry Version: 1.0 Scope: MAR-40 participating teams at UHN, UCL, McGill University, and other authorized collaborating sites 1. Purpose and scope This document defines how contributing teams register and describe the clinical and molecular immuno-oncology cohorts used in MAR-40. It establishes a consistent cohort-level source inventory , not a common patient-level data model or an OMOP conversion requirement. The objectives are to: Provide an auditable description of each cohort's origin, scientific scope, and permitted use. Record whether clinical variables and molecular assays are available, and in what form. Capture annotation versions, processing methods, and sample/patient counts with clear definitions. Enable reproducible curation, harmonization, QC, and descriptive cohort summaries across sites. Support collaboration when patient-level or raw files must remain within approved institutional environments. The registry does not authorize transfer or release of data. Permissions are determined by ethics approvals, agreements, source licenses, and institutional policies. 2. Registry structure and record granularity Use config/cohort_registry_template.csv as the shared, machine-readable schema. Maintain the populated cohort registry in an approved location, with only explicitly authorized metadata committed to the repository. Register one row per cohort and source release . If an independently processed cohort release differs substantially in data content or provenance, register it as a separate version. Each row must have a unique registry_id . A cohort is a source-defined analysis population. It may contain multiple treatment arms, tumor types, molecular assays, patients, specimens, and sampling timepoints. Use companion manifests when these cannot be represented accurately by a single row: Source manifest: original files, hashes, locations, access conditions, and source releases. Assay manifest: one row per assay/data object with platform, sample coverage, reference versions, and preprocessing. Mapping log: source-variable-to-MAR-40 mappings, transformations, decisions, and unresolved issues. QC summary: executed checks, outcomes, reviewer decisions, and limitations. Do not combine patient, sample, specimen, or assay counts into a single field. Counts in the registry are descriptive and must specify their unit. 3. Cohort identification and provenance Registry field Description / recording rule registry_id Unique stable identifier for this cohort/release entry. cohort_id Stable MAR-40 cohort identifier; avoid collisions across sites. cohort_name Human-readable published or source name. contributing_site Site responsible for this registry entry (e.g., UHN, UCL, McGill). source_type Publication , Repository , Clinical study , Institutional , or Other . publication_doi DOI when available; otherwise leave blank. source_accession GEO/SRA/EGA/dbGaP or other source accession when applicable. source_reference Publication URL, data-provider reference, or descriptive source ID. Do not record restricted direct-access URLs or credentials in public files. study_design Interventional , Observational , Retrospective , Other , or Unknown as supported. source_release Original source release, dataset version, or documented snapshot. source_retrieval_date Retrieval or receipt date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) if applicable. curator Team/role or approved contact responsible for registration. last_reviewed Last scientific/technical review date ( YYYY-MM-DD ). registry_status Registered , In curation , Harmonized , QC reviewed , or On hold . This is workflow status, not data quality. Use Unknown (or blank where appropriate) when information is not established. Do not fabricate accession numbers, versions, publications, or collection dates. 4. Access classification and permissions Record the access classification based on actual source-level restrictions , not whether a team can currently view a file. Access type Definition Public The source is publicly accessible under stated terms; reuse restrictions may still apply. Controlled access Access requires authorization, a data access request, or contractual/ethics conditions. Private Locally or privately provided data not generally accessible through a public or controlled repository. Mixed Source components have different access classifications; resolve at file/assay level in the source manifest. Unknown Classification cannot yet be confirmed; flag for review. Store the registry fields access_type , access_reference , permitted_processing_location , cross_site_sharing_status , and restrictions_notes . For cross_site_sharing_status , use Permitted , Restricted , Not permitted , or Pending verification ; this is not inferred from access_type . Never commit patient-level restricted data, source credentials, identifiable information, or sensitive agreement details to the public repository. If a field is unsafe to share publicly, maintain it in an approved restricted site-local registry and publish only permitted metadata. 5. Cohort composition and clinical metadata availability Capture distinct counts separately: n_patients : unique individuals within the defined cohort/release. n_samples : unique biological sample identifiers; repeated specimens/timepoints may increase this relative to n_patients . n_assay_profiles : optional count of assay profiles/data columns, if verified. count_notes : data freeze, exclusions, partial-release coverage, or counting assumptions. Use Unknown or blank for unverified counts; zero means a verified count of zero . Capture source-supported characteristics without forcing a cohort into one category if multiple apply. When several categories are present, use a consistent, documented multi-value convention or companion table: Field Guidance cancer_types Source cancer types; mapping to OncoTree Level 1 is documented in the harmonization output. For multiple values, use a documented delimiter (e.g., semicolon) or a companion table; preserve original source labels. cancer_subtypes Source-supported subtypes or OncoTree Level 2 mappings; optional. treatment_regimens Source regimen labels or components; retain original drug names in approved source manifests. treatment_categories Harmonized categories when verified (e.g., PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA4, IO+combo, IO+chemo, IO+targeted). sampling_timepoints Pre , On , Post or source-specific terms, with ambiguity documented. clinical_age_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_sex_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_stage_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_response_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; specify endpoint type in notes. clinical_os_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_pfs_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_notes Relevant endpoint definitions, time origins, study restrictions, and caveats. Availability vs readiness: Yes indicates that relevant data have been identified, not that fields are sufficiently complete or comparable for pooled analysis. Readiness is assessed separately under Quality Control . Do not treat missing/unknown as No . 6. Molecular data inventory and annotations For each cohort, capture the following registry-level molecular metadata. These availability indicators summarize the cohort; the corresponding sample-level fields in the Data Dictionary are rna , rna_info , dna , and dna_info . Do not interpret missing or unverified data as No . Registry field Description / recording rule rna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; RNA data availability at cohort level. dna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; DNA data availability at cohort level. other_assays Other documented modalities, if present; do not infer absence from unreported assays. source_data_level Raw , Processed , Both , or Unknown . assay_notes Available assay types, source processing descriptions, coverage, and relevant limitations. For each assay, document in a separate assay manifest where applicable: Property Minimum documentation Assay identity Platform and assay type (RNA-seq, microarray, WES, WGS, SNV, CNA, etc.). Data representation Raw files, counts, TPM, normalized expression, segments, VCF/MAF, gene-level calls, etc. Linkage Assay sample identifier, biological sample identifier, cohort and patient relationship. Reference genome Assembly/build, when applicable (e.g., GRCh37/hg19 or GRCh38/hg38). Gene annotation Specific GENCODE version when known, or another documented source. Processing Pipeline name, version/commit, normalization, transformation, major parameters and QC results. Coverage Number of samples/profiles associated with the assay. 6.1 GENCODE strategy Document the project's working approach without retroactively assigning an unverified annotation to published data: GENCODE v19 is the principal reference used for applicable published/processed cohorts where harmonization follows the established published-data workflow. GENCODE v40 is the preferred annotation for cohorts with raw-data access that are reprocessed through the approved standardized workflow, when compatible with its reference genome and processing pipeline. Explicitly reported source version: retain and record the annotation release specified by the publication, data provider, or processing documentation. Undocumented source annotation: record Unknown until source evidence or identifier checks establish the actual release. Do not assert that published data used GENCODE v19 solely because it is a common project reference. Record gene identifier conversions, genome-build changes, and relevant compatibility limitations. A GENCODE release alone does not establish which reference genome or quantification method was used. Preserve the source-reported release and validate compatibility before applying an alternative reference. 7. Versioning, quality review, and maintenance Each registry record should be traceable to a source manifest or authorized provider record. When new data arrive: Update the source release and retrieval/receipt information without overwriting the original provenance. Recalculate and document counts from the appropriate grain (patient vs biological sample vs assay profile). Confirm data-access classification and reuse/sharing constraints. Reassess source field availability and molecular methods; record new or changed mappings. Re-run relevant QC checks and record whether outputs remain comparable with the previous release. docs.text: This document defines how contributing teams register and describe the clinical and molecular immuno-oncology cohorts used in MAR-40. It establishes a consistent cohort-level source inventory , not a common patient-level data model or an OMOP conversion requirement. The objectives are to: Provide an auditable description of each cohort's origin, scientific scope, and permitted use. Record whether clinical variables and molecular assays are available, and in what form. Capture annotation versions, processing methods, and sample/patient counts with clear definitions. Enable reproducible curation, harmonization, QC, and descriptive cohort summaries across sites. Support collaboration when patient-level or raw files must remain within approved institutional environments. The registry does not authorize transfer or release of data. Permissions are determined by ethics approvals, agreements, source licenses, and institutional policies.
docs.title: 1. Purpose and scope

docs.text: Use config/cohort_registry_template.csv as the shared, machine-readable schema. Maintain the populated cohort registry in an approved location, with only explicitly authorized metadata committed to the repository. Register one row per cohort and source release . If an independently processed cohort release differs substantially in data content or provenance, register it as a separate version. Each row must have a unique registry_id . A cohort is a source-defined analysis population. It may contain multiple treatment arms, tumor types, molecular assays, patients, specimens, and sampling timepoints. Use companion manifests when these cannot be represented accurately by a single row: Source manifest: original files, hashes, locations, access conditions, and source releases. Assay manifest: one row per assay/data object with platform, sample coverage, reference versions, and preprocessing. Mapping log: source-variable-to-MAR-40 mappings, transformations, decisions, and unresolved issues. QC summary: executed checks, outcomes, reviewer decisions, and limitations. Do not combine patient, sample, specimen, or assay counts into a single field. Counts in the registry are descriptive and must specify their unit.
docs.title: 2. Registry structure and record granularity

docs.text: Registry field Description / recording rule registry_id Unique stable identifier for this cohort/release entry. cohort_id Stable MAR-40 cohort identifier; avoid collisions across sites. cohort_name Human-readable published or source name. contributing_site Site responsible for this registry entry (e.g., UHN, UCL, McGill). source_type Publication , Repository , Clinical study , Institutional , or Other . publication_doi DOI when available; otherwise leave blank. source_accession GEO/SRA/EGA/dbGaP or other source accession when applicable. source_reference Publication URL, data-provider reference, or descriptive source ID. Do not record restricted direct-access URLs or credentials in public files. study_design Interventional , Observational , Retrospective , Other , or Unknown as supported. source_release Original source release, dataset version, or documented snapshot. source_retrieval_date Retrieval or receipt date ( YYYY-MM-DD ) if applicable. curator Team/role or approved contact responsible for registration. last_reviewed Last scientific/technical review date ( YYYY-MM-DD ). registry_status Registered , In curation , Harmonized , QC reviewed , or On hold . This is workflow status, not data quality. Use Unknown (or blank where appropriate) when information is not established. Do not fabricate accession numbers, versions, publications, or collection dates.
docs.title: 3. Cohort identification and provenance

docs.text: Record the access classification based on actual source-level restrictions , not whether a team can currently view a file. Access type Definition Public The source is publicly accessible under stated terms; reuse restrictions may still apply. Controlled access Access requires authorization, a data access request, or contractual/ethics conditions. Private Locally or privately provided data not generally accessible through a public or controlled repository. Mixed Source components have different access classifications; resolve at file/assay level in the source manifest. Unknown Classification cannot yet be confirmed; flag for review. Store the registry fields access_type , access_reference , permitted_processing_location , cross_site_sharing_status , and restrictions_notes . For cross_site_sharing_status , use Permitted , Restricted , Not permitted , or Pending verification ; this is not inferred from access_type . Never commit patient-level restricted data, source credentials, identifiable information, or sensitive agreement details to the public repository. If a field is unsafe to share publicly, maintain it in an approved restricted site-local registry and publish only permitted metadata.
docs.title: 4. Access classification and permissions

docs.text: Capture distinct counts separately: n_patients : unique individuals within the defined cohort/release. n_samples : unique biological sample identifiers; repeated specimens/timepoints may increase this relative to n_patients . n_assay_profiles : optional count of assay profiles/data columns, if verified. count_notes : data freeze, exclusions, partial-release coverage, or counting assumptions. Use Unknown or blank for unverified counts; zero means a verified count of zero . Capture source-supported characteristics without forcing a cohort into one category if multiple apply. When several categories are present, use a consistent, documented multi-value convention or companion table: Field Guidance cancer_types Source cancer types; mapping to OncoTree Level 1 is documented in the harmonization output. For multiple values, use a documented delimiter (e.g., semicolon) or a companion table; preserve original source labels. cancer_subtypes Source-supported subtypes or OncoTree Level 2 mappings; optional. treatment_regimens Source regimen labels or components; retain original drug names in approved source manifests. treatment_categories Harmonized categories when verified (e.g., PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA4, IO+combo, IO+chemo, IO+targeted). sampling_timepoints Pre , On , Post or source-specific terms, with ambiguity documented. clinical_age_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_sex_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_stage_available Yes , No , or Unknown . clinical_response_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; specify endpoint type in notes. clinical_os_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_pfs_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; does not imply valid paired time/event observations. clinical_notes Relevant endpoint definitions, time origins, study restrictions, and caveats. Availability vs readiness: Yes indicates that relevant data have been identified, not that fields are sufficiently complete or comparable for pooled analysis. Readiness is assessed separately under Quality Control . Do not treat missing/unknown as No .
docs.title: 5. Cohort composition and clinical metadata availability

docs.text: For each cohort, capture the following registry-level molecular metadata. These availability indicators summarize the cohort; the corresponding sample-level fields in the Data Dictionary are rna , rna_info , dna , and dna_info . Do not interpret missing or unverified data as No . Registry field Description / recording rule rna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; RNA data availability at cohort level. dna_available Yes , No , or Unknown ; DNA data availability at cohort level. other_assays Other documented modalities, if present; do not infer absence from unreported assays. source_data_level Raw , Processed , Both , or Unknown . assay_notes Available assay types, source processing descriptions, coverage, and relevant limitations. For each assay, document in a separate assay manifest where applicable: Property Minimum documentation Assay identity Platform and assay type (RNA-seq, microarray, WES, WGS, SNV, CNA, etc.). Data representation Raw files, counts, TPM, normalized expression, segments, VCF/MAF, gene-level calls, etc. Linkage Assay sample identifier, biological sample identifier, cohort and patient relationship. Reference genome Assembly/build, when applicable (e.g., GRCh37/hg19 or GRCh38/hg38). Gene annotation Specific GENCODE version when known, or another documented source. Processing Pipeline name, version/commit, normalization, transformation, major parameters and QC results. Coverage Number of samples/profiles associated with the assay.
docs.title: 6. Molecular data inventory and annotations

docs.text: Document the project's working approach without retroactively assigning an unverified annotation to published data: GENCODE v19 is the principal reference used for applicable published/processed cohorts where harmonization follows the established published-data workflow. GENCODE v40 is the preferred annotation for cohorts with raw-data access that are reprocessed through the approved standardized workflow, when compatible with its reference genome and processing pipeline. Explicitly reported source version: retain and record the annotation release specified by the publication, data provider, or processing documentation. Undocumented source annotation: record Unknown until source evidence or identifier checks establish the actual release. Do not assert that published data used GENCODE v19 solely because it is a common project reference. Record gene identifier conversions, genome-build changes, and relevant compatibility limitations. A GENCODE release alone does not establish which reference genome or quantification method was used. Preserve the source-reported release and validate compatibility before applying an alternative reference.

docs.text: MAR-40 Quality Control Framework Version: 1.0 Scope: Clinical, sample, treatment, outcome, and molecular data curated by MAR-40 collaborating teams at UHN, UCL, McGill, and other authorized sites 1. Purpose and guiding principles This document establishes consistent, traceable quality-control (QC) procedures for MAR-40 cohort curation and harmonization. Participating sites apply the same validation concepts and reporting conventions while processing restricted datasets inside authorized environments. The framework is variable- and analysis-oriented ; conversion to OMOP is not required. The goal is to distinguish three questions: Is the source documented? Can the source, access permissions, file versions, record grain, and relevant clinical/molecular definitions be verified? Is the harmonization correct? Are identifiers, values, units, transformations, annotation releases, and sample links consistent with the Data Dictionary ? Is the result fit for its intended analysis? Are necessary values and endpoint/assay definitions sufficiently complete and comparable for the specific analysis being considered? Guiding principles Preserve source records in approved storage; never overwrite original values during harmonization. Do not convert NA , Unknown , or an absent assessment into No , 0 , non-response, or a censored event. Do not resolve clinical or biological ambiguity by guessing. Record evidence and flag unresolved cases. Assess QC at the correct record grain (cohort, patient, sample, treatment episode, response assessment, or assay). Report counts and denominators . Distinguish samples from unique cohort-patients. QC status describes the readiness of a particular output for a declared purpose , not a blanket judgment of cohort quality. Keep local, restricted row-level issue files separate from shareable summaries; release only what data permissions allow. 2. QC stages and responsibilities Stage Input Main checks Output A. Source QC Original source tables, files, publication/provider documentation Provenance, permissions, file integrity, source schema, identifiers, assay definitions Source manifest and source QC findings B. Post-harmonization QC Standardized clinical/sample/treatment tables and mapping log Target schema, transformations, controlled values, missingness, consistency, endpoint definitions Clinical QC and mapping-issue summaries C. Integration QC Molecular assay files, sample mappings, optional SE/MAE objects Sample linkage, feature IDs, annotation/build, matrix dimensions, assay provenance Molecular/integration QC summary D. Release review QC results, issues, manifests, outputs Outstanding blocking findings, documented limitations, authorized destination Cohort QC disposition and reviewer record Responsibilities: The contributing site's curator executes and documents checks. Site scientific/data leads review clinically important ambiguities and access restrictions. The MAR-40 harmonization team maintains shared rules and evaluates cross-cohort comparability. Changes to the shared rules follow the SOP's version-control process. 3. QC finding severity and cohort dispositions Finding severity and cohort disposition are different fields and must not be conflated. Finding severity Meaning Typical action Error Violates a required integrity, identity, security, or validated data-contract rule Correct or place the affected output on hold Review Scientific meaning, mapping, compatibility, or linkage is ambiguous Investigate; document interpretation and reviewer decision Info Expected missingness, study limitation, or nonblocking deviation Quantify and disclose; retain for analysis planning The final cohort/output disposition is one of: Pass: Applicable checks completed without unresolved blocking findings; essential provenance is available. Pass with documented limitations: Data are usable for a stated purpose but have nonblocking limitations that are recorded and reviewed. Hold for review: Blocking integrity/access problems or material unresolved mapping/endpoint/assay conflicts remain. Do not set an arbitrary global missingness cutoff for all clinical variables. Relevance and acceptable completeness depend on the analysis, source design, and documented study requirements. Absence of a non-applicable or unreported optional field is not, by itself, a blocking error. 4. Source files, access, and provenance Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity if violated SRC-01 Cohort recorded in the cohort registry and source manifest Stable cohort identifier, source/provider, version, curator, and site Error SRC-02 Access status verified Confirm file-level Public , Controlled access , or Private classification and supporting permissions; cohort-level Mixed requires component-level classification and Unknown requires review Error / Review SRC-03 Inputs readable and traceable Filenames/locations, source revision, format, and checksums when permitted Error SRC-04 Original data preserved Source inputs not silently edited or overwritten Error SRC-05 Schema and record grain documented Each table identifies whether rows are patients, samples, visits, treatments, or assays Review SRC-06 Approved execution and output destination Restricted data remain in authorized institutional environments Error Record missing source documentation explicitly. Do not assert a version, license, approval, or source interpretation that cannot be verified. A cohort-level Mixed access classification is acceptable only when each component has a verified access status; Unknown must be resolved before authorizing release. 5. Clinical and sample metadata QC 5.1 Identifiers and record structure Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity ID-01 cohort and identifier availability Nonmissing identifiers required for each table's record grain Error ID-02 Patient keys (cohort, patientid) uniquely identifies patient-level records; repeats are permitted in sample/longitudinal tables Error for invalid grain ID-03 Sample keys (cohort, sampleid) uniquely identifies sample-level records; multiple assays per sample are allowed in an assay-grain table Error for invalid grain ID-04 Patient–sample linkage Each sample resolves to a documented cohort-patient; missing or many-to-many relationships reviewed Error / Review ID-05 Treatment and assessment episodes Distinct treatments/timepoints are not accidentally collapsed or counted as independent patients Review ID-06 Patient attributes across samples Conflicting nonmissing age/sex/disease values are identified and assessed in context of timepoint and record meaning Review Patient counts must be reported using distinct (cohort, patientid) keys . Do not assume patientid is globally unique across cohorts without verified identity linkage. Apparent differences in treatment, response, or disease status across visits or sampling timepoints are not automatically patient-level conflicts; review them at the correct assessment or treatment-episode grain. 5.2 Missingness and valid values Assess missingness for every harmonized core variable at its correct grain. Use an explicit denominator: for example, n_missing / n_patients for a patient-level field and n_missing / n_samples for a sample-level field. When cohorts contain longitudinal assessments, report missingness by relevant timepoint/episode rather than only after flattening. Recognize documented missing representations (e.g., blank, NA , N/A , Unknown , Not recorded ), but retain distinguishable missingness reasons where known ( Not assessed , Not reported , Not applicable , Restricted , Unresolved ). An observed negative value is not missing. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity CLN-01 Target schema Field names/types align with dictionary; approved aliases are mapped explicitly Error / Review CLN-02 Missingness Counts and denominators reported per cohort, variable, grain, and relevant timepoint Info CLN-03 Demographics Numeric age in years, plausible for study context; sex codes supported by source Review CLN-04 Cancer classification cancer_type aligned to documented OncoTree Level 1; Level 2 cancer_subtype only where supported Review CLN-05 Stage/histology Original definition and applicable classification/version retained Review CLN-06 Treatment Regimen/components/targets support standardized category; combination rules traceable Review CLN-07 Sampling timing Pre / On / Post only when source chronology or definition supports assignment Review CLN-08 Access metadata Canonical access_type documented; legacy access type mapped through explicit adapter Review Unrecognized values must be reported, not silently discarded, mapped to Other , or converted to missing. Use Other only where the dictionary and source evidence support that designation. 5.3 Response and survival outcomes Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity OUT-01 RECIST response recist values/assessment criteria (e.g., CR/PR/SD/PD or evaluability status) documented with criteria version/timepoint Review OUT-02 Binary response response definition documented; not automatically derived from RECIST or clinical benefit Review OUT-03 OS/PFS time Nonnegative numeric values in months , with source unit and conversion recorded Error / Review OUT-04 Event indicator event_occurred_os / event_occurred_pfs explicitly recoded to verified 1 = event , 0 = censored Error / Review OUT-05 Time/event pairing Count records with both valid duration and event indicator for each endpoint Info / Review OUT-06 Endpoint definition Time origin, event definition, censoring and follow-up context documented; incompatible definitions flagged Review OUT-07 Longitudinal interpretation Ensure response/survival endpoints link to appropriate patient and, if applicable, treatment episode Review Two distinct metrics must be reported: Metadata availability: A cohort has OS/PFS metadata if at least one patient has a nonmissing duration or event field. This is the rule used in the existing clinical-availability heatmap. Record-level endpoint completeness: A patient/episode has complete OS/PFS fields only when a valid duration and its corresponding verified event indicator are present. Analysis readiness requires additional checks for endpoint meaning, origin, and suitability of the analysis population. Avoid treating a cohort's observed median time as Kaplan–Meier median survival or median follow-up without the relevant statistical method. 6. Molecular assay and annotation QC Core molecular metadata QC uses four fields: rna and dna report assay availability ( Yes , No , or missing), while rna_info and dna_info describe the technology and processing information when available. A missing assay is not automatically a failed QC check, and No must be source-supported. Rules MOL-02 through MOL-08 apply only to relevant molecular data and do not add required core dictionary fields. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity MOL-01 Assay inventory RNA/DNA presence ( rna , dna ) separate from assay description ( rna_info , dna_info ) Review MOL-02 Assay identity Sample IDs and assay IDs traceable to approved sample metadata Error / Review MOL-03 Molecular format and scale Counts/TPM/microarray/variants/CNA data distinguished; normalization and transformations documented Review MOL-04 Reference and gene annotations Genome build, gene ID scheme, and GENCODE or other annotation releases recorded or explicitly Unknown Review MOL-05 Feature and sample integrity Matrix dimensions, duplicate feature/sample IDs, missing rows/columns, feature metadata and sample names checked Error / Review MOL-06 Cross-assay compatibility Build/identifier/version differences explicitly reconciled; no implicit gene-ID or genome-build mixing Review MOL-07 Mutation/CNA representations Variant type, reference build, caller/filter versions, CNA representation and binary-call rules traceable Review MOL-08 SE/MAE validation where used assay dimensions align with rowData / colData ; sampleMap maps assays to correct cohort-patients Error / Review GENCODE policy: For applicable published processed datasets, GENCODE v19 is the historical MAR-40 harmonization reference; do not assign GENCODE v19 when the true source annotation is unverified . For available raw datasets that are reprocessed using MAR-40 standardized pipelines, prefer GENCODE v40 with its compatible reference genome. Where a publication/provider specifies another release, retain the documented source version. Track the source release, genome build, pipeline, and any conversion or feature remapping. Different gene annotations or expression scales are not automatically comparable. For microarrays, retain the source platform, normalization, probe mapping and annotation release; do not describe normalized microarray signals as TPM. Clinical-only cohorts do not need an artificial assay or MAE object. 7. Mapping quality and cross-cohort comparability The dictionary uses Direct , Conditional , Needs review , and Unmapped as mapping statuses. A status describes a mapping decision ; it is not the same as a QC severity or a cohort disposition. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity MAP-01 Source-to-target traceability Source name, original value/code, grain, definition, rule ID and target field retained Error / Review MAP-02 Verified transformations Recode, merge, join, unit conversion or derived value documented and reproducible Error / Review MAP-03 Unresolved mappings Needs review / Unmapped values retained in issue log and excluded from unsupported derived interpretations Review MAP-04 Controlled vocabulary versioning OncoTree, treatment mappings, gene annotation and other resource releases recorded Review MAP-05 Cohort comparability Relevant endpoint definition, treatment context, assay scale, genome build and sampling design assessed for each analysis Review MAP-06 Rule consistency Common transformations have identical versions and semantics across contributing sites Review Cross-cohort comparability should be evaluated for the intended scientific use case . A variable can be syntactically standardized but remain biologically or clinically incomparable; the issue must be visible to analysts. 8. Standard QC reports and output contract Each cohort should generate or document the following artifacts when applicable and permitted . These are recommended names consistent with the SOP ; a shareable aggregate report can be substituted for restricted row-level outputs. <cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Sources, access, versions and authorized paths ├── mapping_log.tsv # Variable-/value-level mapping rules and decisions ├── qc_summary.tsv # One row per QC check, with findings and denominators ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Issue details and decisions, in approved storage ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Assay types and processing/annotation provenance, if present └── run_manifest.txt # Code/environment/input provenance These filenames define the recommended full QC reporting contract ; they are not all outputs of the currently implemented workflow. The Snakemake cohort visualization workflow currently generates descriptive figures and reports, including cohort_summary.csv , cohort_variable_missingness.csv , and patient_level_conflicts.csv . Those outputs support cohort review but do not implement all rule IDs or replace source-level, molecular, and endpoint-specific QC. Additional recommended QC views may be produced from the same checks: missingness_summary.tsv , patient_sample_validation.tsv , endpoint_completeness.tsv , and molecular_qc_summary.tsv . Keep one canonical issue log, rather than conflicting copies with different statuses. 8.1 qc_summary.tsv columns Column Meaning cohort Cohort identifier qc_stage Source , Harmonized , Integration , or Release rule_id Stable identifier defined in this document or a versioned rule configuration domain Identity, clinical, outcome, molecular, provenance, mapping, etc. record_grain Cohort, patient, sample, assay, episode, etc. n_checked Number of eligible records checked n_flagged Number of records or instances flagged for this check severity Error , Review , or Info check_status Pass , Flagged , or Not applicable description Concise finding/interpretation issue_log_ref Local pointer to issue record(s), where permitted rule_version QC-rule implementation version run_id Identifier linking the result to the run manifest For rules that apply once per cohort or file, use the appropriate grain and denominator; do not report percentages without explaining the checked population. A flagged finding does not necessarily mean the entire cohort is on hold. 8.2 unresolved_issues.tsv columns Recommended fields: issue_id , cohort , rule_id , affected_grain , affected_record_key (local/restricted where needed), description , severity , mapping_status (if relevant), evidence , proposed_action , owner , reviewer , review_date , resolution , issue_status , run_id . Store patient-level identifiers or sensitive source values only in approved storage. Share sanitized aggregates or non-identifying issue summaries when authorized. 8.3 run_manifest.txt minimum content Record input source IDs and versions/checksums where permitted; workflow/script and Git commit; data dictionary and mapping versions; environment lockfile or package versions; configuration, run date, site/curator, authorized output path, and QC rule version. Re-running against the same permitted inputs and versions should regenerate the QC outputs without manual edits to the final tables. 9. Review and release procedure Execute the applicable QC checks on source, harmonized, and integrated data, as supported by the cohort's modalities. Inspect every Error and clinically material Review finding; document fixes, scientific interpretation, or explicit limitations. Re-run affected checks after code, mapping, or data corrections; preserve the run/version history. Assign a disposition ( Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review ) for the specific output and intended analysis. Record the designated reviewer and decision , including the output/dataset version, intended use, review date, unresolved limitations, and any restrictions; confirm that sharing and destination are authorized before any cross-site release. Release only approved outputs with their manifests and permissible QC summaries. A held cohort need not be discarded: the relevant issue may affect only a particular assay or endpoint. The release decision should specify what is usable, restricted, pending review, or excluded from a stated analysis. Curation and harmonization QC checklist [ ] Source identity, provenance, access classification and permissions documented. [ ] Required identifiers valid at the correct grain; patient–sample links checked. [ ] Harmonized fields validated against the versioned dictionary. [ ] OncoTree cancer classification and treatment-group mappings reviewed. [ ] Response and OS/PFS definitions, units, event coding and completeness checked. [ ] RNA/DNA assay metadata, GENCODE/source annotation, genome build and processing provenance reviewed where applicable. [ ] SE/MAE and sampleMap validated if created. [ ] Missingness and mapping issues reported with counts, denominators and dispositions. [ ] QC outputs and run manifest saved in approved storage, with the correct version identifiers. [ ] Relevant site reviewer decision and permitted release destination documented. 10. Maintenance and change control The MAR-40 harmonization team maintains this framework alongside the SOP and Data Dictionary . New validation rules must include a stable rule_id , objective, input grain, expected result, severity, implementation version, and examples/test cases. Changes that alter clinical interpretations, mapping categories, endpoint comparability or assay processing require review by the relevant scientific/data leads. Record changes in Git; preserve enough version information to reproduce earlier QC results. If a rule change affects previously released cohorts, assess whether outputs should be regenerated and document that decision. This document defines the QC specification ; executable implementations and configuration are maintained with the workflows described in Usage . Source QC Original source tables, files, publication/provider documentation Provenance, permissions, file integrity, source schema, identifiers, assay definitions Source manifest and source QC findings B. docs.title: 2. QC stages and responsibilities

docs.text: Finding severity and cohort disposition are different fields and must not be conflated. Finding severity Meaning Typical action Error Violates a required integrity, identity, security, or validated data-contract rule Correct or place the affected output on hold Review Scientific meaning, mapping, compatibility, or linkage is ambiguous Investigate; document interpretation and reviewer decision Info Expected missingness, study limitation, or nonblocking deviation Quantify and disclose; retain for analysis planning The final cohort/output disposition is one of: Pass: Applicable checks completed without unresolved blocking findings; essential provenance is available. Pass with documented limitations: Data are usable for a stated purpose but have nonblocking limitations that are recorded and reviewed. Hold for review: Blocking integrity/access problems or material unresolved mapping/endpoint/assay conflicts remain. Do not set an arbitrary global missingness cutoff for all clinical variables. Relevance and acceptable completeness depend on the analysis, source design, and documented study requirements. Absence of a non-applicable or unreported optional field is not, by itself, a blocking error.
docs.title: 3. QC finding severity and cohort dispositions

docs.text: Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity if violated SRC-01 Cohort recorded in the cohort registry and source manifest Stable cohort identifier, source/provider, version, curator, and site Error SRC-02 Access status verified Confirm file-level Public , Controlled access , or Private classification and supporting permissions; cohort-level Mixed requires component-level classification and Unknown requires review Error / Review SRC-03 Inputs readable and traceable Filenames/locations, source revision, format, and checksums when permitted Error SRC-04 Original data preserved Source inputs not silently edited or overwritten Error SRC-05 Schema and record grain documented Each table identifies whether rows are patients, samples, visits, treatments, or assays Review SRC-06 Approved execution and output destination Restricted data remain in authorized institutional environments Error Record missing source documentation explicitly. Do not assert a version, license, approval, or source interpretation that cannot be verified. A cohort-level Mixed access classification is acceptable only when each component has a verified access status; Unknown must be resolved before authorizing release.
docs.title: 4. Source files, access, and provenance

docs.text: Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity ID-01 cohort and identifier availability Nonmissing identifiers required for each table's record grain Error ID-02 Patient keys (cohort, patientid) uniquely identifies patient-level records; repeats are permitted in sample/longitudinal tables Error for invalid grain ID-03 Sample keys (cohort, sampleid) uniquely identifies sample-level records; multiple assays per sample are allowed in an assay-grain table Error for invalid grain ID-04 Patient–sample linkage Each sample resolves to a documented cohort-patient; missing or many-to-many relationships reviewed Error / Review ID-05 Treatment and assessment episodes Distinct treatments/timepoints are not accidentally collapsed or counted as independent patients Review ID-06 Patient attributes across samples Conflicting nonmissing age/sex/disease values are identified and assessed in context of timepoint and record meaning Review Patient counts must be reported using distinct (cohort, patientid) keys . Do not assume patientid is globally unique across cohorts without verified identity linkage. Apparent differences in treatment, response, or disease status across visits or sampling timepoints are not automatically patient-level conflicts; review them at the correct assessment or treatment-episode grain.
docs.title: 5.1 Identifiers and record structure

docs.text: Assess missingness for every harmonized core variable at its correct grain. Use an explicit denominator: for example, n_missing / n_patients for a patient-level field and n_missing / n_samples for a sample-level field. When cohorts contain longitudinal assessments, report missingness by relevant timepoint/episode rather than only after flattening. Recognize documented missing representations (e.g., blank, NA , N/A , Unknown , Not recorded ), but retain distinguishable missingness reasons where known ( Not assessed , Not reported , Not applicable , Restricted , Unresolved ). An observed negative value is not missing. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity CLN-01 Target schema Field names/types align with dictionary; approved aliases are mapped explicitly Error / Review CLN-02 Missingness Counts and denominators reported per cohort, variable, grain, and relevant timepoint Info CLN-03 Demographics Numeric age in years, plausible for study context; sex codes supported by source Review CLN-04 Cancer classification cancer_type aligned to documented OncoTree Level 1; Level 2 cancer_subtype only where supported Review CLN-05 Stage/histology Original definition and applicable classification/version retained Review CLN-06 Treatment Regimen/components/targets support standardized category; combination rules traceable Review CLN-07 Sampling timing Pre / On / Post only when source chronology or definition supports assignment Review CLN-08 Access metadata Canonical access_type documented; legacy access type mapped through explicit adapter Review Unrecognized values must be reported, not silently discarded, mapped to Other , or converted to missing. Use Other only where the dictionary and source evidence support that designation.
docs.title: 5.2 Missingness and valid values

docs.text: Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity OUT-01 RECIST response recist values/assessment criteria (e.g., CR/PR/SD/PD or evaluability status) documented with criteria version/timepoint Review OUT-02 Binary response response definition documented; not automatically derived from RECIST or clinical benefit Review OUT-03 OS/PFS time Nonnegative numeric values in months , with source unit and conversion recorded Error / Review OUT-04 Event indicator event_occurred_os / event_occurred_pfs explicitly recoded to verified 1 = event , 0 = censored Error / Review OUT-05 Time/event pairing Count records with both valid duration and event indicator for each endpoint Info / Review OUT-06 Endpoint definition Time origin, event definition, censoring and follow-up context documented; incompatible definitions flagged Review OUT-07 Longitudinal interpretation Ensure response/survival endpoints link to appropriate patient and, if applicable, treatment episode Review Two distinct metrics must be reported: Metadata availability: A cohort has OS/PFS metadata if at least one patient has a nonmissing duration or event field. This is the rule used in the existing clinical-availability heatmap. Record-level endpoint completeness: A patient/episode has complete OS/PFS fields only when a valid duration and its corresponding verified event indicator are present. Analysis readiness requires additional checks for endpoint meaning, origin, and suitability of the analysis population. Avoid treating a cohort's observed median time as Kaplan–Meier median survival or median follow-up without the relevant statistical method.
docs.title: 5.3 Response and survival outcomes

docs.text: Core molecular metadata QC uses four fields: rna and dna report assay availability ( Yes , No , or missing), while rna_info and dna_info describe the technology and processing information when available. A missing assay is not automatically a failed QC check, and No must be source-supported. Rules MOL-02 through MOL-08 apply only to relevant molecular data and do not add required core dictionary fields. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity MOL-01 Assay inventory RNA/DNA presence ( rna , dna ) separate from assay description ( rna_info , dna_info ) Review MOL-02 Assay identity Sample IDs and assay IDs traceable to approved sample metadata Error / Review MOL-03 Molecular format and scale Counts/TPM/microarray/variants/CNA data distinguished; normalization and transformations documented Review MOL-04 Reference and gene annotations Genome build, gene ID scheme, and GENCODE or other annotation releases recorded or explicitly Unknown Review MOL-05 Feature and sample integrity Matrix dimensions, duplicate feature/sample IDs, missing rows/columns, feature metadata and sample names checked Error / Review MOL-06 Cross-assay compatibility Build/identifier/version differences explicitly reconciled; no implicit gene-ID or genome-build mixing Review MOL-07 Mutation/CNA representations Variant type, reference build, caller/filter versions, CNA representation and binary-call rules traceable Review MOL-08 SE/MAE validation where used assay dimensions align with rowData / colData ; sampleMap maps assays to correct cohort-patients Error / Review GENCODE policy: For applicable published processed datasets, GENCODE v19 is the historical MAR-40 harmonization reference; do not assign GENCODE v19 when the true source annotation is unverified . Where a publication/provider specifies another release, retain the documented source version. Track the source release, genome build, pipeline, and any conversion or feature remapping. Different gene annotations or expression scales are not automatically comparable. For microarrays, retain the source platform, normalization, probe mapping and annotation release; do not describe normalized microarray signals as TPM. docs.title: 6. Molecular assay and annotation QC

docs.text: The dictionary uses Direct , Conditional , Needs review , and Unmapped as mapping statuses. A status describes a mapping decision ; it is not the same as a QC severity or a cohort disposition. Rule ID Check Expected outcome Default severity MAP-01 Source-to-target traceability Source name, original value/code, grain, definition, rule ID and target field retained Error / Review MAP-02 Verified transformations Recode, merge, join, unit conversion or derived value documented and reproducible Error / Review MAP-03 Unresolved mappings Needs review / Unmapped values retained in issue log and excluded from unsupported derived interpretations Review MAP-04 Controlled vocabulary versioning OncoTree, treatment mappings, gene annotation and other resource releases recorded Review MAP-05 Cohort comparability Relevant endpoint definition, treatment context, assay scale, genome build and sampling design assessed for each analysis Review MAP-06 Rule consistency Common transformations have identical versions and semantics across contributing sites Review Cross-cohort comparability should be evaluated for the intended scientific use case . docs.title: 7. Mapping quality and cross-cohort comparability

docs.text: Each cohort should generate or document the following artifacts when applicable and permitted . These are recommended names consistent with the SOP ; a shareable aggregate report can be substituted for restricted row-level outputs. <cohort_id>/ ├── source_manifest.tsv # Sources, access, versions and authorized paths ├── mapping_log.tsv # Variable-/value-level mapping rules and decisions ├── qc_summary.tsv # One row per QC check, with findings and denominators ├── unresolved_issues.tsv # Issue details and decisions, in approved storage ├── assay_manifest.tsv # Assay types and processing/annotation provenance, if present └── run_manifest.txt # Code/environment/input provenance These filenames define the recommended full QC reporting contract ; they are not all outputs of the currently implemented workflow. docs.title: 8. Standard QC reports and output contract

docs.text: Column Meaning cohort Cohort identifier qc_stage Source , Harmonized , Integration , or Release rule_id Stable identifier defined in this document or a versioned rule configuration domain Identity, clinical, outcome, molecular, provenance, mapping, etc. record_grain Cohort, patient, sample, assay, episode, etc. n_checked Number of eligible records checked n_flagged Number of records or instances flagged for this check severity Error , Review , or Info check_status Pass , Flagged , or Not applicable description Concise finding/interpretation issue_log_ref Local pointer to issue record(s), where permitted rule_version QC-rule implementation version run_id Identifier linking the result to the run manifest For rules that apply once per cohort or file, use the appropriate grain and denominator; do not report percentages without explaining the checked population. A flagged finding does not necessarily mean the entire cohort is on hold.
docs.title: 8.1 qc_summary.tsv columns

docs.text: Recommended fields: issue_id , cohort , rule_id , affected_grain , affected_record_key (local/restricted where needed), description , severity , mapping_status (if relevant), evidence , proposed_action , owner , reviewer , review_date , resolution , issue_status , run_id . docs.title: 8.2 unresolved_issues.tsv columns

docs.text: Record input source IDs and versions/checksums where permitted; workflow/script and Git commit; data dictionary and mapping versions; environment lockfile or package versions; configuration, run date, site/curator, authorized output path, and QC rule version. Re-running against the same permitted inputs and versions should regenerate the QC outputs without manual edits to the final tables.
docs.title: 8.3 run_manifest.txt minimum content

docs.text: Execute the applicable QC checks on source, harmonized, and integrated data, as supported by the cohort's modalities. Inspect every Error and clinically material Review finding; document fixes, scientific interpretation, or explicit limitations. Re-run affected checks after code, mapping, or data corrections; preserve the run/version history. Assign a disposition ( Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review ) for the specific output and intended analysis. Record the designated reviewer and decision , including the output/dataset version, intended use, review date, unresolved limitations, and any restrictions; confirm that sharing and destination are authorized before any cross-site release. Release only approved outputs with their manifests and permissible QC summaries. A held cohort need not be discarded: the relevant issue may affect only a particular assay or endpoint. The release decision should specify what is usable, restricted, pending review, or excluded from a stated analysis.
docs.title: 9. Review and release procedure

docs.text: [ ] Source identity, provenance, access classification and permissions documented. [ ] Required identifiers valid at the correct grain; patient–sample links checked. [ ] Harmonized fields validated against the versioned dictionary. [ ] OncoTree cancer classification and treatment-group mappings reviewed. [ ] Response and OS/PFS definitions, units, event coding and completeness checked. [ ] RNA/DNA assay metadata, GENCODE/source annotation, genome build and processing provenance reviewed where applicable. [ ] SE/MAE and sampleMap validated if created. [ ] Missingness and mapping issues reported with counts, denominators and dispositions. [ ] QC outputs and run manifest saved in approved storage, with the correct version identifiers. [ ] Relevant site reviewer decision and permitted release destination documented.
docs.title: Curation and harmonization QC checklist

docs.text: The MAR-40 harmonization team maintains this framework alongside the SOP and Data Dictionary . New validation rules must include a stable rule_id , objective, input grain, expected result, severity, implementation version, and examples/test cases. Changes that alter clinical interpretations, mapping categories, endpoint comparability or assay processing require review by the relevant scientific/data leads. Record changes in Git; preserve enough version information to reproduce earlier QC results. If a rule change affects previously released cohorts, assess whether outputs should be regenerated and document that decision. This document defines the QC specification ; executable implementations and configuration are maintained with the workflows described in Usage .

docs.text: MAR-40 Usage Guide Version: 1.0 Scope: Participating MAR-40 collaborators at UHN, UCL, and McGill University 1. Purpose This guide describes how collaborators will prepare and run reproducible clinical and molecular data harmonization workflows for MAR-40. It complements the Data Curation SOP , Data Dictionary , Quality Control Framework , and Data Sources Guide . The repository uses Pixi for environment management and is intended to use Snakemake to coordinate data preparation, harmonization, quality control (QC), and integration. Commands shown as planned below must be validated against the repository's actual pixi.toml / pixi.lock , Snakefile , and rule definitions before they are treated as runnable. The workflow must be executable inside each site's approved computing environment. The presence of code or documentation does not authorize the movement of controlled-access or private data between institutions. 2. Two reference examples The repository will provide two approved, shareable example cohorts to demonstrate different assay configurations. Example Available inputs Intended outputs Example 1: Clinical + RNA Clinical metadata, RNA expression, patient-to-sample mapping Harmonized clinical metadata and RNA matrix, QC reports, provenance, optional RNA MAE Example 2: Clinical + RNA + DNA Clinical metadata, RNA expression, DNA alteration data, patient-to-sample mapping Harmonized clinical metadata, RNA and DNA data, QC reports, provenance, optional multi-assay MAE Examples should contain synthetic data or data explicitly authorized for public redistribution . They should illustrate realistic source-specific variable names, missing values, and repeated patient samples. They must not contain direct patient identifiers. Assay availability is explicit: Example 1 does not require or generate DNA files. DNA processing is enabled only for cohorts where DNA inputs are declared. 3. Prerequisites and environment Git, to obtain the repository and track code versions. Pixi , to install the locked project environment. Snakemake, R, Python, and Bioconductor dependencies as declared by the project's environment configuration . Read/write permissions for the selected local input and output locations. From a terminal, clone the repository (or use an existing checkout): git clone https://github.com/bhklab/mar40-data-harmonization.git cd mar40-data-harmonization pixi install pixi install assumes the checkout includes a valid Pixi manifest. Do not install additional untracked package versions as a substitute for the agreed project environment; document any site-specific changes. 4. Input data contract Provide a cohort-specific configuration that identifies all available data and their formats. The paths and filenames below illustrate a proposed example layout; they are not assertions that these files already exist. data/ rawdata/ examples/ example_clinical_rna/ clinical.csv rna_expression.tsv sample_map.csv example_clinical_rna_dna/ clinical.csv rna_expression.tsv dna_alterations.tsv sample_map.csv procdata/ results/ 4.1 Clinical metadata The source file should contain a documented patient identifier, and any additional fields available for cancer type, histology, stage, age, sex, treatment, response, survival, and sampling timepoints. The source file does not need to use standardized column names : mappings to the MAR-40 target variables must be documented according to the Data Dictionary . Treat (cohort, patientid) as the unique patient key for cohort-level summaries unless a validated cross-cohort linkage exists. Preserve original source values in the approved environment; do not silently replace unrecognized codes. Document survival units, time origin, and event/censoring conventions before transformation. Missing optional clinical data are reported as missing, not treated as negative observations. 4.2 RNA expression Document whether the input is counts, TPM, another normalized expression scale, or microarray data. Capture the platform, gene identifier system, genome build when relevant, normalization method, transformation, reference annotation release, and sample identifiers. MAR-40 generally uses GENCODE v19 for applicable published/processed datasets and GENCODE v40 for standardized reprocessing when raw data are available ; when a publication or source supplies a specific annotation release, retain that documented information. Do not assume a dataset used v19 solely because it is published or its annotation is unknown. Any gene-ID or genome-build conversion must be traceable. 4.3 DNA alterations (Example 2 only) Document the actual assay and input representation (for example, SNV/indel calls, CNA segments, or a curated alteration matrix). Capture the genome build, variant annotation and filtering methods, sample IDs, and rules used to produce a gene-by-sample representation. Do not assume all DNA datasets contain both SNV and CNA data. 4.4 Patient-to-sample linkage A sample mapping file or equivalent verified linkage must associate each assay sample with its clinical patient. Multiple samples per patient and different sample availability across assays are permitted, but ambiguous or unmatched IDs must be reported by QC. 5. Cohort-specific configuration Use an explicit configuration rather than detecting DNA availability only by the presence of a filename. For example, a proposed YAML configuration is: cohorts: example_clinical_rna: clinical: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/clinical.csv sample_map: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/sample_map.csv rna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna/rna_expression.tsv units: source_documented annotation: source_documented dna: enabled: false example_clinical_rna_dna: clinical: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/clinical.csv sample_map: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/sample_map.csv rna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/rna_expression.tsv units: source_documented annotation: source_documented dna: enabled: true file: data/rawdata/examples/example_clinical_rna_dna/dna_alterations.tsv representation: source_documented genome_build: source_documented The final schema, mapping-file paths, and workflow target names must match the implemented Snakefile and shared config before execution. 6. Workflow stages For either example, the intended sequence is: Register inputs: record cohort, provenance, access classification, source version, available assays, and input checksums where permitted. Harmonize clinical data: apply versioned source-to-target mappings, controlled values, and unit conversions. Prepare molecular assays: validate identifiers and measurement scales; process RNA and, only where declared, DNA. Validate linkages: check clinical IDs, assay sample IDs, and patient-to-sample relationships. Integrate data: construct appropriate harmonized tables and, where supported, a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE). Run QC: generate missingness, mapping, consistency, assay, and integration checks. Record provenance: capture input versions, code commit, environment, rule versions, exceptions, and output locations. QC checks should flag uncertain mappings rather than silently dropping records. Final release or permitted sharing follows the access conditions and review process defined in the SOP. 7. Running Snakemake The commands below are illustrative targets for implementation , not currently verified executable commands. Before publishing them as operational instructions, confirm that pixi.toml includes Snakemake and that the repository contains a valid Snakefile with appropriate rules and targets. # Example: inspect the workflow without executing it pixi run snakemake --cores 4 --dry-run # Example: execute the configured default targets pixi run snakemake --cores 4 For site-specific execution, the finalized workflow should support selecting a cohort and approved local input/output paths through configuration. Do not hard-code individual workstation paths or require controlled datasets to be copied into the Git repository. 8. Expected output and QC records For each cohort, aim to produce the following artifacts where applicable and permitted : <approved_output_root>/<cohort_id>/ clinical_harmonized.csv rna_harmonized.* dna_harmonized.* # Only if DNA is provided sample_map_validated.csv integrated_mae.rds # If produced by the workflow source_manifest.tsv mapping_log.tsv qc_summary.tsv unresolved_issues.tsv run_manifest.txt The naming convention is a proposed output contract. The exact filenames, assays, and serialization formats should be fixed in the workflow implementation and reflected in the SOP and QC documentation. Record QC outcomes as Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review , as defined by the Quality Control Framework . A cohort-level availability summary is not equivalent to analytical readiness. 9. Reproducibility and cross-site collaboration For each run, preserve or reference: Source dataset version and approved location; checksums when allowed. Cohort configuration and applied mapping-rule version. Git commit and Pixi lockfile/environment details. RNA/DNA processing parameters, annotation resources, and software versions. QC results, unresolved mappings, permitted outputs, curator/reviewer information, and execution date. The same workflow should produce structurally comparable outputs at UHN, UCL, and McGill without requiring raw or controlled datasets to cross institutional boundaries. 10. Troubleshooting and implementation status Issue Recommended action Required input missing Verify the cohort configuration and approved path. Unexpected clinical value Check source definition; record the unmapped value and request review. RNA gene IDs differ across datasets Verify gene-ID type, GENCODE release, and explicit conversion rules. Sample IDs fail to join Inspect sample mapping, duplicated IDs, and cohort-level namespaces. Missing DNA for Example 1 Expected; confirm dna.enabled: false . Snakemake reports no Snakefile or missing rule The workflow is not yet implemented or the working directory is incorrect. Restricted input cannot be shared Execute locally within an approved environment; share only authorized outputs. Implementation checklist: Before calling the example workflows runnable, add approved example datasets, finalize the input/output contracts, implement and test Snakemake rules, validate the Pixi environment, and confirm expected QC reports for both assay configurations. Update this guide with the exact tested commands and expected results. Document history Version Date Status Summary 1.0 November 20, 2026 Active guide; workflow implementation pending Defines two example cohorts, input contracts, proposed Pixi/Snakemake execution, outputs, QC, and cross-site reproducibility requirements.

docs.text: The commands below are illustrative targets for implementation , not currently verified executable commands. Before publishing them as operational instructions, confirm that pixi.toml includes Snakemake and that the repository contains a valid Snakefile with appropriate rules and targets. # Example: inspect the workflow without executing it pixi run snakemake --cores 4 --dry-run # Example: execute the configured default targets pixi run snakemake --cores 4 For site-specific execution, the finalized workflow should support selecting a cohort and approved local input/output paths through configuration. Do not hard-code individual workstation paths or require controlled datasets to be copied into the Git repository.
docs.title: 7. Running Snakemake

docs.text: For each cohort, aim to produce the following artifacts where applicable and permitted : <approved_output_root>/<cohort_id>/ clinical_harmonized.csv rna_harmonized.* dna_harmonized.* # Only if DNA is provided sample_map_validated.csv integrated_mae.rds # If produced by the workflow source_manifest.tsv mapping_log.tsv qc_summary.tsv unresolved_issues.tsv run_manifest.txt The naming convention is a proposed output contract. The exact filenames, assays, and serialization formats should be fixed in the workflow implementation and reflected in the SOP and QC documentation. Record QC outcomes as Pass , Pass with documented limitations , or Hold for review , as defined by the Quality Control Framework . A cohort-level availability summary is not equivalent to analytical readiness.
docs.title: 8. Expected output and QC records

docs.text: For each run, preserve or reference: Source dataset version and approved location; checksums when allowed. Cohort configuration and applied mapping-rule version. Git commit and Pixi lockfile/environment details. RNA/DNA processing parameters, annotation resources, and software versions. QC results, unresolved mappings, permitted outputs, curator/reviewer information, and execution date. The same workflow should produce structurally comparable outputs at UHN, UCL, and McGill without requiring raw or controlled datasets to cross institutional boundaries.
docs.title: 9. Reproducibility and cross-site collaboration

docs.text: Issue Recommended action Required input missing Verify the cohort configuration and approved path. Unexpected clinical value Check source definition; record the unmapped value and request review. RNA gene IDs differ across datasets Verify gene-ID type, GENCODE release, and explicit conversion rules. Sample IDs fail to join Inspect sample mapping, duplicated IDs, and cohort-level namespaces. Missing DNA for Example 1 Expected; confirm dna.enabled: false . Snakemake reports no Snakefile or missing rule The workflow is not yet implemented or the working directory is incorrect. Restricted input cannot be shared Execute locally within an approved environment; share only authorized outputs. Implementation checklist: Before calling the example workflows runnable, add approved example datasets, finalize the input/output contracts, implement and test Snakemake rules, validate the Pixi environment, and confirm expected QC reports for both assay configurations. Update this guide with the exact tested commands and expected results.

The workflow invokes the existing workflow/scripts/clinical_visualization.R and expects an already harmonized, comma-delimited, sample-level table containing cohort , patientid , and sampleid . The script accepts input and output paths as its first two positional arguments. The synthetic example lives at data/examples/MAR40_synthetic_sample_level.csv and is suitable for testing; restricted clinical data must remain in approved institutional storage. Missing fields (e.g. all-missing age or stage , partially missing response ) are permitted. Interpret F/M , R/NR , CR/PR/SD/PD/NE , and NA using the MAR-40 data dictionary. This workflow does not perform source-specific harmonization, determine data-access rights, or verify that OS/PFS are analysis-ready. The environment must also provide Rscript and the R dependencies ggplot2 , dplyr , tidyr , and ComplexHeatmap to the shell; validate package availability using Rscript -e 'sapply(c("ggplot2","dplyr","tidyr","ComplexHeatmap"), requireNamespace, quietly=TRUE)' . Pixi tasks and package definitions have not been verified against your local pixi.toml . To run a different harmonized CSV, add a dataset under datasets: in config/visualization.yaml (or provide a separate local config via --configfile ). Each dataset writes to its own results subfolder.
